newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to hand back nationalised property.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to hand back nationalised property.

text.p: Croatia enacted legislation on Friday to return property nationalised during the 1945-90 Yugoslav communist era to former owners or provide them alternative compensation.
The law applies to property confiscated from private citizens between May 15, 1945 and June 25, 1990, the Croatian state news agency HINA said.
Confiscated property will be returned to the former owner, and if this proves impossible, the former owner will be entitled to money or securities compensation.
People living in once nationalised flats will be allowed to buy them with former owners given proper compensation.
"I am satisfied that injustice has now been at least partly corrected -- injustice that was not committed by this state," Justice Minister Miroslav Separovic said on state television.
The law is to be used by Croatian citizens only -- either former owners or their legitimate heirs.

According to Justice Ministry data, 25,059 individuals have submitted applications for return of property. Of those, 1,805 applications were for firms, 49,229 for land, 1,961 for movable goods, 29,414 for flats, and 16,189 for business premises.
The law comes into force on January 1.
